require_capability_resolution.reason: Refuses a mission step whose required capability is unresolved. The CAPABILITY_REQUIRED flow it belongs to is PLAN Wave 6 (parent mission blocks, genesis child mission produces the capability, parent resumes); until that flow exists there is no caller with a capability to resolve.

require_lifecycle_state.reason: Genesis lifecycle state precondition. The genesis machine runs today through its own transition table; this helper is the alternative entry point. PLAN Wave 6 merges the genesis and tool_registry lifecycles onto one vocabulary - route it or drop it there, not before.

validate_file.reason: REASON REPLACED 2026-09-09. The previous one said 'Operator-facing CLI surface with no CLI verb attached - give it one or delete it', which reads as dead code. It is not. validate_file is the ENGINE of the V4 narrative-shape invariant: tests/invariants/v4/test_phase_v4_b_narrative_shape.py:62,66 runs it over every agent file to enforce the pedagogy contract, and that test is a real gate. pedagogy_lint.py (which does run in CI) only mentions this module in a comment; it does not import it. So the consumer is an invariant test, which is this control's INTENDED and sufficient consumer -- there is no unguarded production path here to close. The reachability gate cannot express that distinction: its rule that 'tests calling a control directly cannot count as evidence' is right for a control meant to run in production and wrong for one whose gate IS the invariant. Third instance of the CONTROL_VERBS classification problem, after record_resolution (a real control the prefix list cannot see) and check_remaining_budget (an accessor it wrongly called a control, since renamed). Open decision is whether the gate learns 'invariant-driven control' as a category, not whether to delete this.

validate_generated_adapter.reason: Skill-genesis adapter validation. The adapter authoring loop is dispatched through the convergent drafting agents, and the kernel-side validation of their output is not yet on that path - which is precisely the shape of defect this gate exists to surface, on a lane that is not live.

validate_request.reason: Date replaced 2026-09-09; the reason was RE-VERIFIED and stands. The request half of the aria/agent-request/v1 contract. Its counterpart validate_response is live with 11 production callsites; this one has none, because no production code produces that envelope -- the live dispatch path mints aria/agent-invocation-request/v1 instead. Wiring a validator to a vocabulary nothing speaks would enforce a shape against zero traffic and read as coverage. The blocked work is ORPHAN-MEDIUM-572's own: reconcile the two envelope vocabularies against their real producers FIRST, then enforce. Deliberately not deleted -- unlike the duplicate entry points removed today, this one has no live sibling answering its question; it is the only validator for a contract half.

verify_adapter_imports.reason: Sandbox check for a generated adapter's import set. Same dormant skill-genesis lane as validate_generated_adapter; the three sandbox checks are one decision.

verify_adapter_signature.reason: Sandbox check for a generated adapter's entry-point signature. Same dormant skill-genesis lane; wire with its siblings or not at all.

verify_branch_tip.reason: Auto-merge head-SHA freshness check. merge_pr_if_ready performs its own head-SHA freshness comparison inline, so the protection exists; this is the extracted helper that the inline code never adopted. PLAN Wave 8 implements branch_tip_lock_and_recheck as a real hard-fail check - that is where these two collapse into one.

verify_workflow_registry.reason: REASON REPLACED 2026-09-09, and the previous one was FALSE. It claimed 'the equivalent assertion runs in CI as a TypeScript invariant, so the drift IS caught - by the other lane'. Checked: no spec under tests/invariants references WORKFLOW_CONTRACTS, and the nearest one (aria-kernel-workflow-setup.spec.ts) asserts something else entirely -- that a job running kernel code provisions the kernel first. Deleting on that reason would have removed an UNDUPLICATED guarantee: preflight's live verify_workflow_contract validates ONE contract against its YAML and by construction only ever visits workflows that already have a contract, so an ARIA workflow added with neither a contract nor an audited exclusion is invisible to it. Only the whole-inventory verdict sees that. Wiring it into verify_workflow_preflight was attempted and REVERTED: that preflight legitimately runs against synthetic workspaces, where the workflow YAMLs are absent and the inventory verdict is invalid for a reason that is not a defect (test_workflow_enterprise_preflight proved it). A repo-wide invariant needs a caller that always sees the real repo, and neither a CLI verb nor a CI step exists for it yet -- that entry point is the open decision, not whether the control is worth keeping. Verified valid=True against the live tree on 2026-09-09, so it will pass the day it is wired.
